summary: Klickitat County DNR lookout: 40-foot tower in 1958, two-story cab on concrete base in 1977, removed or destroyed in 1995; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1995; sources differ on which word fits

access.note: No source describes how the site is reached today

events.note: State crew built a road to the summit in July 1957 for a proposed lookout site

Two-story lookout building on a concrete base replaced the tower; register says a 10-foot concrete base with DNR cab
Register says removed; Willhite says removed or destroyed
FireLookout.com and the Weebly page say destroyed

corrections.proposed: Remove height_m, or record 12.2 m (40 ft) against the 1958 tower only
corrections.why: 12.2 m is 40 feet, the height of the 1958 wooden tower. No source gives a height for the 1977 two-story cab, and Neal's 1960 account describes a 30-foot tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, the Weebly page and Willhite give 40 feet; Neal's 1960 account, as reprinted by Willhite, says 30 feet. The story reports both.
The register and Willhite say removed (Willhite adds removed or destroyed); firelookout.com and the Weebly page say destroyed. The story reports both.

sources.title: Everybody has a story: Fire tower duty put girl on top of world

notes_for_editor: No source describes the site today. The Columbian article is paywalled; only its intro was readable, and the 1960 account is taken from Willhite's reprint. The brief's elevation (941.2 m) and coordinates match the register. The brief's two_story kind describes the 1977 cab, so it is kept. Staffing as_of 1995 marks the end of the structure; the only documented staffing is the 1960 summer. The height_m correction is proposed, not applied to the record.
